subject: Literature
title: Digital Censorship and the Great Firewall
description: A quick, practical guide to Digital Censorship and the Great Firewall.

hook.text: China's Great Firewall blocks over eight hundred million internet users from accessing most foreign websites and books.

buildup.text: Algorithms scan for banned keywords, and human censors delete posts containing political criticism within minutes.

discovery.text: Chinese citizens use coded language and memes to evade censorship, creating a new digital form of samizdat.

twist.text: When censors banned Winnie the Pooh for resembling the president, the ban itself became international news.

climax.text: Digital censorship is faster and more comprehensive than anything in history, but creative resistance adapts just as fast.

punchline.text: The internet made censorship faster but resistance more creative.

quiz.question: How do Chinese citizens evade digital censorship?
options: They use satellite internet that bypasses the firewall
They use coded language and memes as a new form of digital samizdat
They cannot evade it at all
